name: CloudCruise

modes.label: Automation hours ($3/h after 2 free hours, Starter)

sizes.name: automation hour (VM, proxies and AI included)

modes.note: cloudcruise.com/pricing 2026-09-28: Starter free, "2 automation hours, then $3/hour"; "1 automation hour = 60 minutes of workflow runtime. VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included." Browser CPU/RAM not published. Scale ($700/mo) overage not published, so this regime is bound to Starter.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: 2 automation hours included, then $3/h. Up to 3 seats. Standard BAA. Unlimited workflows, versioning/rollbacks, maintenance agent. Whether the 2 hours reset monthly is not stated.

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: $700/month; priority support, unlimited seats; included hours / overage not published.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Enterprise: custom pricing. Adds (over Scale) SSO, RBAC, audit logs, reserved browser instances, custom SLAs, DPA, custom MSA; bring-your-own proxy is Enterprise-only.

plans.name: Accelerate
plans.note: Custom/month. Everything in Scale plus dedicated workflow build support, white-glove migration, human maintenance fallback.

features.ip_note: Proxies included in the automation-hour price but OFF by default per workflow; managed pool selectable as random, static (closest to a target IP) or by country; bring-your-own proxy URL is Enterprise only. Proxy type (residential/datacenter) not documented.

caveats: Starter ($0/month, up to 3 seats) includes 2 automation hours then $3/hour. Scale is $700/month (unlimited seats, volume discounts; included hours and overage rate not published). Accelerate and Enterprise are custom-priced. Workflow maintenance and model runtime differ from raw browser hosting. CPU/RAM unspecified.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Priced as unsized automation-hours ($3/h includes AI usage and proxies, so it is not comparable to a raw browser or VM hour). Concurrency limits not published.

Product is now positioned for healthcare automation (payer portals, EHR, RCM, credentialing) and announced as generally available. Run video/screenshots/logs retained 30 days (custom retention on Scale). ToS: subscriptions auto-renew; fees non-refundable; billed via Stripe.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.tiers: Concurrency not published; runs beyond capacity are queued ('Smart queueing'); 'Reserved browser instances' only on Enterprise.
fleet.notes: API rate limits per API key (workspace): 500 req/1 s, 1,000/15 s, 2,000/60 s. Homepage animation shows 'Active sessions allowed: 3 / Queued 6' (illustrative marketing graphic, not a stated limit).

harness_api.quote: Fully deterministic; every run follows the same graph.
harness_api.note: The Run API starts runs of a pre-built deterministic workflow graph with input variables (webhook events, live view, interrupt, submit user-interaction/input), not a prompt-driven agent harness. The Builder Agent that turns a prompt into a workflow is started in the dashboard ('Open a new workflow in the dashboard and describe the task.'). The open-source CLI + 'cloudcruise install --skills' lets Claude Code/Cursor on YOUR machine manage workflows, not a harness inside CloudCruise.

secret_proxy.quote: The agent uses it, and immediately zeroises the buffer.
secret_proxy.note: Vault: client-side AES-256-GCM encrypted credentials (username/password/TOTP secret; optional 1Password binding resolved at run time) are decrypted in memory and typed into login forms by the browser agent inside the worker; 2FA codes via the CC 2FA Proxy (SMS/email/magic link). Not an outbound-request credential-injection proxy; the secret is present in the worker at runtime.

image_oci.quote: 1 automation hour = 60 minutes of workflow runtime. VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — CloudCruise runs a managed browser-automation worker for your workflow graph; there is no way to boot a customer-supplied OCI/Docker image.

docker_inside.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shell/container access inside the browser worker is exposed; interaction is limited to the workflow DSL nodes.

nested_virt.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no /dev/kvm or general compute access is exposed to customers.

desktop.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — CloudCruise exposes a live view of the browser session (iframe-embeddable), not a general-purpose VNC/RDP graphical desktop.

computer_use.quote: execution: Execution type: STATIC (UI: "Static"), LLM_VISION (UI: "AI (Screenshot)"), or COORDINATES (UI: "Coordinates")
computer_use.note: not offered as a customer-facing API: screenshot-based clicking (LLM_VISION/COORDINATES) is an internal execution mode CloudCruise's own browser agent uses inside its workflow DSL; there is no first-party API letting a customer's own agent drive an arbitrary desktop via screenshots+clicks.

ssh.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no SSH access to the underlying browser worker is documented or offered.

snapshot.quote: Enable Cookies and Local Storage in your Vault entry to reuse sessions
snapshot.note: Session/auth state (cookies, local storage) can be persisted and reused across runs at the application level via the Vault, but there is no disk- or memory-level machine snapshot/restore feature exposed to customers.

snapshot_auto.quote: Enable Cookies and Local Storage in your Vault entry to reuse sessions
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no automatic full-machine snapshot/restore on stop; only opt-in cookie/localStorage session reuse.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no API/CLI to checkpoint the worker machine itself; 'debug-snapshots' in the Run API refers to per-node execution debug data, not a machine snapshot.

fork.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no machine-cloning feature; concurrency is handled by spinning up new workers per run, not by forking a machine.

fork_running.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — see fork.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no machine forking of any kind is documented.

pause_resume.quote: 1 automation hour = 60 minutes of workflow runtime.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — billing is per automation-hour of workflow runtime; there is no pause/resume of the underlying worker machine.

wake_on_request.quote: This event is sent when a run is queued and waiting for an available worker.
wake_on_request.note: Runs are queued and dispatched to a fresh/pooled worker on demand ('Smart queueing'), which is workflow-run scheduling, not a stopped/sleeping persistent machine that wakes on an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no customer-attached persistent disk/filesystem; only Vault-stored credentials/session data and run artifacts (screenshots/videos/logs) persist.

volume_attach.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no attachable volumes documented.

volume_shared.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shared-volume feature documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: 1 automation hour = 60 minutes of workflow runtime.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — workers are provisioned per run rather than left running idle for a customer to auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no customer-selectable CPU/RAM sizing is exposed at all, let alone live resize.

agent_harnesses.note: The open-source CLI adds skills so coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor) running on the USER's own machine can manage CloudCruise workflows; this is not a coding-agent harness preinstalled/running inside a CloudCruise-hosted sandbox.

own_agent_api.note: The Run API is a first-party API that starts/streams/interrupts runs of CloudCruise's own browser-automation agent (Builder/Maintenance agents driving the workflow graph) — this is the provider's own task agent, not a customer's coding harness.

mcp_server.quote: CloudCruise docs index (Quickstart, Workflows, Run API, SDKs: TypeScript, Python, CLI)
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is listed among CloudCruise's SDKs/CLI/docs; integration is via REST Run API, TypeScript/Python SDKs, webhooks, and a CLI — no mention of an MCP server.

public_ipv4.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no customer-addressable machine with its own public IPv4; only outbound (egress) proxy IPs are relevant.

inbound_https.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no inbound HTTPS URL to reach a port on the worker; access is via the Run API/webhooks/live-view iframe, not inbound networking to the machine.

ingress_rules.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no inbound port exposure exists to control.

egress_allowlist.quote: If sing-box (the OS-level proxy router) dies mid-session, the worker fails the run rather than reverting to direct internet egress. This protects compliance use cases where all automation traffic must stay inside the customer's network.
egress_allowlist.note: CloudCruise enforces routing of a workflow's outbound (target-site) traffic through a configured proxy and fails closed instead of falling back to direct egress, which is a provider-side outbound restriction (fail-closed proxy enforcement) for compliance.

egress_http_rules.quote: Target-site traffic flows through your proxy.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: egress control is proxy-routing based (whole-connection), not documented at HTTP method/path granularity.

guest_firewall.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — customers get no root/shell access to configure iptables/nftables inside the worker.

static_egress_ip.quote: static | target IP address | The managed proxy closest to that IP — ideal for geo-restricted content or region-specific testing
static_egress_ip.note: The 'static' managed-proxy mode picks a proxy geographically closest to a target IP for consistency of region, not a guaranteed fixed/dedicated outbound IP assigned per customer; a truly fixed IP is only available by bringing your own proxy (Enterprise).

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — CloudCruise is a browser-workflow-automation platform; no GPU machines are offered.

windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no customer-facing Windows machine option; CloudCruise automates target web/Citrix apps via a browser, it does not sell Windows VMs.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machines offered.

arm64.quote: VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — compute architecture is not customer-selectable; no ARM option documented.

self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — CloudCruise is a hosted SaaS; only the CLI and language SDKs (client libraries) are distributed as open-source, not the core automation platform.

byoc.quote: Enterprise: Custom SLAs, Data processing agreement, Custom MSA
byoc.note: No BYOC/dedicated-VPC deployment option is documented, even at the Enterprise tier; Enterprise adds SSO/RBAC/audit/SLA/DPA terms, not deployment into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.note: Only the CLI and SDK client libraries (cloudcruise-cli, cloudcruise-js, cloudcruise-python) are open source; the core workflow/browser-automation platform itself is closed-source SaaS.

eu_data_residency.note: CloudCruise is positioned around US healthcare compliance (HIPAA Business Associate Agreements on every plan, payer-portal/EHR/RCM/credentialing use cases) and no page in the docs, pricing, or marketing site mentions EU/Europe regions, GDPR, or any data-residency/region selection option. Treated as not offered given the exclusively US-healthcare-compliance framing and total absence of any region concept in the product.

isolation.quote: 1 automation hour = 60 minutes of workflow runtime. VM infrastructure, proxies, and AI usage are all included.
isolation.note: Pricing page states each automation hour's runtime includes 'VM infrastructure', i.e. each browser worker/session runs inside its own VM, but no docs page names the specific hypervisor (firecracker/qemu-kvm/cloud-hypervisor/etc.), so classified generically as dedicated-vm rather than a specific microVM technology.
